一个稍微不同的问题，但 Tom Scott 做过一个很棒的视频，讲 YouTube 版权系统的自动化：[VIDEO] 总而言之，自动版权检查解决了大多数版权问题，其程度是其他任何方案都难以真正提供的。虽然存在少量（但非常不公平的）误报，但系统整体带来的收益远远超过这一负面影响：为了让 YouTube 存在下去！关于事实核查，我更想知道，在那些简单明了的案例中（地平说、气候变化等），有多少读过这类“事实标记”的人真的改变了看法。说实话，“真正的真相”这个问题也许永远无法解决，但无能之辈的成因也同样不会消失。
comments.text: > youtube algo's screwing up content creator A slightly different problem, but Tom Scott did an excellent video on the automation of the copyright system on YouTube: [VIDEO] In summary, auto copyright checking solves Most copyright issues, to a degree that no other solution can really provide. And while there are a small (yet very unfair) number of false positives, the benefit that the system as a whole allows far outpaces that downtrend: for YouTube to exist! With regards to fact checking, I'd be more interested to hear how many people who read those kind of "fact flags" actually change their opinion in an easy case (flat earth, climate change, etc.). Honestly, the problem of "true truth" might never be solved, but so will the cause of incompetence never disappear.

The World's Is.》[VIDEO]。总的来说我同意 OP 的看法（他们显然有权发布自己的表演并从中获利），但我发现，关于 YouTube 版权主张系统的大多数评论甚至都没有承认这个问题的主要方面。也许 YouTube 事实上的垄断在这里帮了倒忙，而且很难把“大型自助发布视频平台”的问题和 YouTube 特有的问题分开。如果没有 YT 目前这样的系统，它绝对会被正当的版权投诉告到倾家荡产。这在很多方面是版权法没有考虑到现代技术而设计的问题。我认为一个很好的第一步，是让版权所有者因大范围过度主张权利而受到惩罚。
comments.text: I recommend the excellent video by Youtuber Tom Scott "YouTube's Copyright System Isn't Broken. The World's Is." [VIDEO] While I agree with the OP in broad strokes (they clearly have the right to post and profit off their performance), I find that the vast majority of comments on Youtube's copyright claim system fail to even acknowledge major aspects of the problem. Perhaps Youtube's practical monopoly does it a disservice here, and it's hard to separate "big self publishing video platform" problems with Youtube specific problems. Without a system like YT currently has, it would get absolutely sued into oblivion by rightful copyright complaints. This is in many ways is a problem of copyright law not being designed with modern technology in mind. I think a good first step would be a way for copyright owners to be punished for broadly overreaching with their claims.

comments.author: sillysaurusx
comments.story_title: Google Play keeps banning the same web browser due to vague DMCA notices
comments.why_zh: 用来支持该系统并非为现代设计的说法。
comments.quote_zh: 这个系统不是为现代设计的。
comments.text_zh: 目前，补救办法不是惩罚发起方，而是提交反通知。我跟 Meta 打过这个流程。很糟，而且把我项目早期的势头给毁了。但我们提交之后一两周内就恢复了。这个系统看起来可能不公平。它确实不公平。但这是我们现有的最好的办法，因为这个系统不是为现代设计的。[VIDEO] 我们能有提交反通知这样的救济手段，已经算幸运了。我一直想做个非营利组织，把反通知作为一种服务提供。基本上就是让人捐款，然后每当某个人的项目（比如这个倒霉的网页浏览器）收到 DMCA 主张时，他们就能获得起草并提交反通知的帮助。请律师来做这事不便宜，但你基本必须请，这是最不公平的地方。发起下架的公司资源雄厚，而被盯上的对象往往什么都没有。这个想法工作量可能太大了，但总得有人做。我们需要一个为创作者撑腰的组织。或者至少有一个组织，能给创作者足够的法律绳索去自己上吊——如果提出主张的实体决定起诉的话，这有时确实是真实可能。但创作者应该能自己决定要不要承担这个风险，而不必先付几千美元。
comments.text: The remedy isn’t (currently) to punish the issuer. It’s to file a counter notice. I’ve been through this process against Meta. It sucked, and killed my project’s early momentum. But it was restored within a week or two after we filed. It may seem like this system isn’t fair. It certainly isn’t. But it’s the best we have, because the system was not designed for the modern era. [VIDEO] It’s lucky we even have a recourse like filing a counter notice. I’ve wanted to make a non profit that offers up counter notices as a service. Basically, let people donate, and whenever someone’s project (like this unfortunate web browser) gets issued a DMCA claim, they’d be able to get a counter notice drafted and filed. It’s not cheap to hire a lawyer to do it, but you pretty much have to, which was the most unfair part. The companies filing the takedowns have lots of resources, but the targets often have substantially none. That idea is probably too much work, but someone should do it. We need an organization to go to bat for creators. Or at least an organization that gives the creator enough legal rope to hang themselves if the entity making the claim decides to file a lawsuit, which is sometimes a real possibility. But the creator should get to decide whether to take on that risk without having to pay thousands of dollars first.

comments.author: hn_acker
comments.story_title: Copyright is not a moral right, it's a monetization strategy
comments.why_zh: 在关于 DMCA 改革的讨论中被链接；未表示背书。
comments.text_zh:
总体而言，版权法——包括像 DMCA 512（17 U.S. Code § 512 [1]）这样面向在线的部分——需要对虚假版权侵权主张（包括带有疏忽/无人工审核的自动化批量举报）设定有实际意义的处罚，其力度与相应侵权处罚相比最多只小一个数量级。（同等力度可能会吓退太多财富较少的作者，使他们不敢提起正当的侵权诉讼。）目前，即使你以 fair use 抗辩成功打赢侵权诉讼，律师费和诉讼费仍会把你拖垮。权利人发出 DMCA 侵权通知只需要出于善意，即使该主张最终被证明明显虚假；然而，针对虚假侵权主张提交 counter notice 的人却要在伪证罪处罚下提交 [2]。与此同时，当前的安全港标准要求提供用户上传内容的服务提供商，仅凭针对该材料的侵权主张，就尽快删除材料 [1]：
> 在收到第 (3) 段所述侵权主张通知后，迅速删除或禁用对据称侵权或属于侵权活动标的之材料的访问。
再说一次，这些侵权通知可能是自动生成的，也可能是胡扯 [3]（不管有意与否），但服务提供商必须照做才能避免第三方责任。明显的结果就是过度屏蔽。安全港标准应该被修改。
comments.text: Copyright law in general, including online-oriented parts such as DMCA 512 (17 U.S. Code § 512 [1])), needs meaningful penalties for false copyright infringement claims (including automated mass reports with negligent/no human review) that are no more than one magnitude smaller than what would be the corresponding penalties for infringement. (Equal magnitude might intimidate too many lower-wealth authors from filing rightful infringement suits.) Currently, successfully fighting an infringement lawsuit with a fair use defense will still ruin you because of the attorney fees and court fees. A DMCA infringement notice requires only good faith from the rightsholder even if the claim turns out to be patently false, yet someone filing a counter notice against a false infringement claim does so under penalty of perjury [2]. Meanwhile, the current safe harbor standard requires service providers with user-uploaded content to remove material as soon as possible solely based on a claim of infringement with respect to that material [1]: > upon notification of claimed infringement as described in paragraph (3), responds expeditiously to remove, or disable access to, the material that is claimed to be infringing or to be the subject of infringing activity. Again, these infringement notices can be automated or BS [3] (whether intentional or not), but the service provider has to comply to avoid third-party liability. The obvious result is overblocking. > 我隐约记得 Tom Scott 说过类似的话，作为他有一次使用 small claims court 的例子？Tom Scott 在《YouTube's copyright system isn't broken. The world's is.》[0] 中说了关于他自己的两件事。
1. “一家泰国电视台拿走了我的一个视频，未经许可在他们某个大型电视节目中播放，然后把整个电视节目放进了 Content ID。结果我的原视频被他们打上了一个 Content ID 命中，这事花了很长时间才解决。”
2. “英国有……Intellectual Property Enterprise Court [1]……而且该法院设有 small claims track。如果你是个人摄影师或视频制作者，你可以……以‘litigant in person’的身份提起诉讼，这是英国人对‘没有律师’的花哨说法。我做过这件事，因为一家大公司盗用了我一个视频。……然后我就那样走进去，没有律师，以为自己有案子可打，以为自己看清了现实。从统计上看，胜算对我不利，但我成功提起了诉讼。那家公司和我和解了，他们付钱让我撤诉，因为他们错了，他们知道自己错了，而且他们知道，只要我做一点工作、交一百多英镑的诉讼费，我就能真的把这事送到法官面前。”
他并没有说这两件事有关联。他并没有说他用法院解决了 Content ID 主张。

comments.text: > I vaguely remember Tom Scott saying something similar as an example of the one time he used a small claims court? Tom Scott said two things about himself in YouTube's copyright system isn't broken. The world's is. [0] 1. "A TV channel from Thailand took one of my videos, played it out without permission in one of their big television shows, and then put that entire television show into Content ID. I got a Content ID hit on my original video from them, and that took a long time to sort out." 2. "The UK has [...] the Intellectual Property Enterprise Court [1][...] and that court has a small claims track. If you're an individual photographer or video maker, you can [...] issue a claim as a "litigant in person", which is the fancy British term for "without a lawyer". I've done it, because a major company ripped off one of my videos. [...] And there I was, walking in, no lawyer, thinking I had a case, thinking I had a grip on reality. Statistically, the odds weren't in my favour, but I filed successfully. And the company settled with me, they paid me to drop the claim, because they were in the wrong, and they knew they were in the wrong, and they knew I could actually get it to a judge in exchange for a bit of work and a court fee of just over £100." He did not say these two incidents were related. He did not say he used a court to resolve a Content ID claim. [0] [VIDEO] [1] [LINK]
